Re: Internal Appeal of Adverse Benefit Determination  
Member: Casey Grant  
Member ID: W903474664  
Plan: CareSource Commercial/ACA Marketplace, West Virginia  
Reference number: POC-C29C7CFC4D-26579  
Requested procedure: Knee arthroscopy with meniscectomy  
CPT: 29881  
Date of denial: August 15, 2026

Dear CareSource Appeals Reviewer:

I am appealing the denial of prior authorization for CPT 29881, knee arthroscopy with meniscectomy. The denial states that the submitted imaging findings do not support medical necessity. The clinical record supports the requested procedure because the MRI documents a displaced bucket-handle tear of the medial meniscus with mechanical locking, and my symptoms and examination demonstrate substantial functional impairment despite extensive conservative treatment.

The relevant clinical evidence is as follows:

- I have had 14 months of progressive knee pain that has not resolved with rest.
- I completed 14 weeks of supervised physical therapy directed at quadriceps strengthening and range of motion, including 24 visits from March 27, 2026, through July 3, 2026. The treatment and completion are documented in the physical therapy discharge note.
- I used NSAIDs for eight months without adequate relief.
- A corticosteroid injection on April 25, 2026, provided only four weeks of partial relief.
- The July 19, 2026 MRI demonstrates a displaced bucket-handle tear of the medial meniscus with mechanical locking.
- I experience locking and giving way, cannot squat or kneel, and am limited to level walking.
- Examination shows positive provocative testing on the affected side, with range of motion limited by pain.
- The MRI shows preserved articular cartilage and Kellgren-Lawrence grade 1 changes. These findings do not explain away the displaced, mechanically symptomatic meniscal tear; instead, they document that the principal structural abnormality is the meniscal tear.
- There is no active infection or untreated substance-use condition. My BMI is 29, and I am a nonsmoker.

The requested surgery is being recommended by Marchetti, MD, an orthopedic surgeon, to address a displaced medial meniscal tear causing mechanical locking after failure of prolonged nonoperative care. The record therefore addresses both the objective imaging abnormality and the associated symptoms, examination findings, functional limitations, and failed conservative treatment.

The public CareSource information I was able to review identifies knee arthroscopy as a musculoskeletal procedure subject to medical-necessity review by TurningPoint Healthcare Solutions, LLC, but I was not able to retrieve the specific clinical guideline or policy document applied to CPT 29881. Accordingly, I am not quoting plan policy language. Please provide the complete guideline or clinical criteria used in this determination, including the specific imaging-related requirement that CareSource believes was not met, and identify the exact portions of the submitted MRI or other records that were considered insufficient.

Please conduct a full reconsideration of this request using the MRI report, physical therapy discharge note, medication history, injection history, orthopedic examination, and functional limitations. I request that CareSource reverse the denial and approve authorization for the medically necessary knee arthroscopy with meniscectomy, CPT 29881.

If CareSource does not reverse the denial, please provide the final written determination, the complete clinical rationale, the criteria applied, and instructions for any available external review or further appeal.

Sincerely,

Casey Grant
